header.title: Nvidia's founder-centric structure makes it a key-man risk with no deep successor bench

s01_bottom_line.text: The article argues Nvidia was built around Jensen personally — a flat kingdom of ~60 direct reports and ~42,000 employees with no deep successor bench, where founder conviction enabled multi-year bets (CUDA, tensor cores) and dealmaking; without him the company 'might be an entirely different beast' and would be materially worse off. ⟨cited figures: approximate⟩
The question that matters for shareholders is what Nvidia is without Jensen; the article concludes it would be materially worse off and the next CEO unlikely to make Jensen's bold bets.

A professional-manager successor answering to the board/shareholders is less likely to sustain Jensen's long-horizon bets, kingmaking and supply-chain mastery, posing a qualitative downside to Nvidia's franchise; the article does not quantify an earnings effect.
